summary.headline: Sun Pharma Q2 FY27 sales rose 11.8% to INR161,000 million, but EBITDA grew only 4.8% and US sales fell 8.2% on lenalidomide erosion and Ilumya slowdown.
summary.overview: Consolidated sales grew 11.8% YoY to INR161,000 million with gross margin at 80.8%, while EBITDA rose 4.8% to INR47,439 million at a 29.3% margin, lower YoY due to a lenalidomide benefit in Q2 FY26. India formulations grew 17.3% to INR55,523 million, ahead of IPM, while US sales declined 8.2% to USD455 million on lenalidomide erosion and a slowdown in Ilumya. Reported PAT was INR19,885 million versus adjusted PAT of INR31,620 million after exceptional items including Organon acquisition costs and a litigation settlement provision. Organon acquisition is on track to close in Q4 FY27 and R&D spend ran below intended levels at 4.8% of sales.

financial_highlights.change: higher YoY on product mix and currency

segments.name: Global Innovative Medicines
segments.commentary: Sales USD356 million, up 6.9%, 21.1% of Sun sales; growth led by Ilumya ex-US, Cequa and Odomzo, with Ilumya slowing in the US.

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Sales INR55,523 million, up 17.3%, 34.5% of consolidated sales; Sun ranked #1 with 8.6% share in Pharmarack MAT Sep-26 vs 8.3% a year earlier; volume growth 6.7% vs IPM 1.8%; 15 new launches in Q2.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Sales USD455 million, down 8.2% YoY (up 6.5% QoQ), 27% of consolidated sales; lenalidomide erosion was the main drag; 5 generic launches in the quarter.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Formulation revenue USD350 million, up 7.6% (7.4% constant currency), 20.7% of consolidated revenue; Ilumya growing in Romania and Brazil; partner launched semaglutide generics in Brazil.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Formulation revenue USD241 million, higher YoY, about 14.3% of consolidated revenue; growth lower than EM and not separately guided.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: management will stick to the revenue guidance given at the start of the year (high single digit), despite H1 growth of about 11%.
R&D spend running below intended levels; management expects a significant ramp-up in H2 and to meet the full-year guidance of 6% to 7% of sales.
Organon acquisition on track to close in Q4 FY27; borrowing cost expected in line with Organon's current weighted average cost of debt; goodwill not yet estimated.
Further acquisition-related exceptional costs expected until day one of the Organon deal.
Ilumya expected to return to more typical growth over the next few quarters, helped by the psoriatic arthritis approval and actions taken.
Ilumya psoriatic arthritis soft launch planned for November 2026, with full launch in following months; launch costs built into existing budget.
capex_capacity: Ophthalmic products at the Assam plant: 11 products voluntarily recalled and manufacturing temporarily ceased voluntarily; company says remedial action is underway, and it declined to comment on media reports of a regulator directive.
Management said it is putting infrastructure in place to recruit clinical trial subjects, which is expected to lift R&D spend.
Unloxcyt and Leqselvi launches continue; Nidlegy filed in Europe and awaiting approval.
Lerodalcibep (PCSK9 inhibitor, licensed from LIB Therapeutics) approved in Europe and in pre-launch phase ex-US and ex-China.
demand_pricing: India growth split: management said roughly 50% to 60% of India growth comes from volume plus new products, with the rest from pricing.
Ilumya US slowdown attributed to a mix of market factors and execution issues; management said interventions are in place.
Ilumya ranked #2 across all biologics for new patients in 73 main hospitals in Japan.
Unloxcyt elevated to NCCN Category 2A preferred recommendation; long-term data showed complete responses of 34% in locally advanced and 17% to 21% in metastatic CSCC.
Ilumya psoriatic arthritis approved in US (HCP-administered IL-23, quarterly dosing); about one-third of plaque psoriasis patients have comorbid PsA.

US government agreement: Most Favored Nation pricing extended to state Medicaid programs; delays Section 232 tariffs on innovative products by over 2 years and exempts Sun from GLOBE and GUARD Medicare models.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Ilumya slowdown in the US, what actions have been taken, and when will growth recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Richard Ascroft cited a mix of market and execution factors, with interventions already in place; growth expected to return to typical patterns over the next few quarters, helped by the PsA launch, which uses the existing sales force with no extra launch spend.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance being updated given H1 double-digit top-line growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar said the company will stick to the guidance given at the start of the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will R&D ramp up in H2 and will the 6% to 7% full-year target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Shanghvi said R&D spend is expected to ramp significantly in subsequent quarters, tied to clinical trial recruitment, and the company expects to meet overall guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Organon effective cost of borrowing and the goodwill share?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayashree Satagopan said borrowing cost should be in line with Organon's current weighted average cost of debt; goodwill is too early to estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Assam plant ophthalmic issue material?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar declined to comment on media reports, said 11 ophthalmology products were voluntarily recalled and manufacturing temporarily ceased, and said remedial action is underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is the India volume growth sustainable, and how much is semaglutide contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar said growth comes from brand building, field force expansion and launches; he would not say whether it is sustainable and did not give a volume figure excluding semaglutide.

risks_watch: Ilumya US slowdown: US Innovative sales growth depends on recovery over the next few quarters.
Ophthalmic products at Assam plant: recall and manufacturing cessation; regulatory outcome and financial impact unclear.
Organon closing in Q4 FY27 and further one-time acquisition costs in exceptional items; goodwill and debt cost still to be finalised.
R&D underspend in Q2 must catch up in H2 to reach the 6% to 7% of sales guidance.
Lenalidomide erosion continues to weigh on US sales.
Tax rate rose to 28.3% from 24.7% YoY.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India, Unloxcyt and the Organon timeline, but cautious and evasive on the Ilumya slowdown, the Assam plant issue and product-level detail, which management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: Ilumya in treating psoriatic arthritis will be the only IL -23 that is physician administered, making it the perfect choice for patients that require extra care and benefit from HCP administration.
Regarding the guidance, I think we'll stick to what guidance we have given at the beginning of the year.
So I think it's too early for me to comment on it.

growth.why: Management held FY27 revenue guidance at high single digit (about 8% used as midpoint) despite H1 growth of about 11%, with no specific capacity or order numbers backing it; the R&D ramp-up in H2 and Ilumya recovery are stated without quantified timing or capacity, and the Assam ophthalmic plant is halted.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA grew only 4.8% vs sales up 11.8% and margin at 29.3%, lower YoY on lenalidomide benefit in Q2 FY26; R&D ramp-up in H2 (from 4.8% of sales toward 6-7% guidance) and Assam plant disruption weigh on margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity commissioning was guided; the Assam ophthalmic plant has manufacturing temporarily ceased after 11 product recalls, so near-term capacity is reduced rather than added.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India volume grew 6.7% vs IPM 1.8% and 15 launches in Q2, but US sales fell 8.2% to USD455M on lenalidomide erosion and Ilumya slowdown; Ilumya recovery is expected but unquantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and capex was not discussed, so a new capex announcement is not signalled; Organon closing in Q4 FY27 is an acquisition, not organic capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 high-single-digit revenue guidance despite H1 growth of about 11%, signalling no upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: R&D must ramp from 4.8% of sales in Q2 to meet the 6-7% full-year guidance, the Assam plant recall is unresolved, and the Ilumya US slowdown persists; the company, however, said it will stick to guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ilumya psoriatic arthritis soft launch planned for November 2026 with full launch in following months, plus Unloxcyt and Leqselvi launches continuing, Nidlegy awaiting EU approval and lerodalcibep in pre-launch ex-US.

rows.label: Organon acquisition close
rows.why: Management confirmed the deal is on track to close in Q4 FY27 as per earlier timelines; borrowing cost tied to Organon's weighted average cost of debt and goodwill not yet estimated.

rows.label: Assam ophthalmic plant recall and halt
rows.why: 11 products voluntarily recalled and manufacturing temporarily ceased; remedial action underway, and management declined to comment on reports of a regulator directive, so financial impact is unclear.

rows.label: Ilumya US recovery
rows.why: US sales fell 8.2% on lenalidomide erosion and Ilumya slowdown; management expects return to typical growth helped by PsA approval, but gave no quantified timing and the brief flags it as a key risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on India growth, Unloxcyt and the Organon timeline, but cautious on the Ilumya slowdown, the Assam plant recall and product-level detail; analysts pushed on guidance and R&D catch-up, and management held guidance without quantifying the Ilumya recovery.
